messages:
rahul: Pager fired — several KMS decrypts from service-principal 'svc-data-agg' targeting org-secrets/finance-key around 02:12 UTC. Pattern looks cross-workspace. Can someone triage? :eyes:
sofia: saw the alert, pulling audit logs now. any recent RBAC changes?
rahul: we shipped the principal-type canonicalization yesterday as part of the role-refactor rollout (flag: rbac-principal-rewrite=on). rollout started 01:30 UTC.
mike: ugh, that lines up. I remember we changed how service accounts map to workspace membership to dedupe legacy ids. Might have introduced transient inherited roles.
eva: logs: 
```
2025-05-14T02:11:58Z audit: decrypt request, principal=svc-data-agg@prod, token_id=tok_9f3, resolved_principals=[svc-data-agg, svc-legacy-123], effective_roles=[workspace-viewer, org-secrets-reader]
```
seems effective_roles includes org-secrets-reader for some requests.
alex: reproduction steps I ran: toggle rbac-principal-rewrite on in staging and run `rbacctl simulate --principal svc-data-agg --resource projects/alpha/kms/finance-key` result: ALLOW via role inheritance from legacy mapping.
sofia: can someone paste the failing SQL join from the membership resolver? I want to see the merge order.
rahul: snippet from resolver (simplified):
```
SELECT principal_id, role
FROM principal_mappings pm
JOIN role_bindings rb ON rb.bind_to = COALESCE(pm.canonical_id, pm.legacy_id)
WHERE pm.feature_flag = 'rbac-principal-rewrite' OR rb.scope = 'org'
ORDER BY rb.created_at DESC
```
note the ORDER BY caused newer rewrite mappings to appear after older legacy bindings in some shards. That made COALESCE pick the wrong id during the merge window.
mike: so race: on some nodes pm.canonical_id NULL -> COALESCE chooses legacy_id; on others canonical present -> binds to workspace-level roles that accidentally pick up org-level binding via duplicate role rows.
eva: immediate mitigation: rollback flag? If we flip rbac-principal-rewrite=off the canonical mapping stops being used, but that doesn't undo the merged bindings.
sofia: recommended quick steps: 1) revoke active tokens for svc-data-agg (invalidate caches), 2) rotate the KMS key binding (create new key version + rotate consumer key policy), 3) set emergency deny policy on org-secrets for svc-data-agg.
rahul: doing token revoke now: `authctl revoke --principal svc-data-agg --all`
sec-bot: Automated action: revoked 12 tokens for principal svc-data-agg (request id: rb-20250514-001).
mike: I'm pushing a hotfix to the membership resolver to prefer canonical_id if present before joining role_bindings. patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/commit/0f3a9fb (will deploy to canary in 10m).
alex: also we need an audit query to list principals that had conflicting canonical vs legacy ids during the migration window (01:20-02:40 UTC).
eva: wrote a query: `SELECT principal, COUNT(*) as conflicts FROM principal_mapping_audit WHERE canonical_id IS NOT NULL AND legacy_id != canonical_id AND ts BETWEEN '2025-05-14T01:20Z' AND '2025-05-14T02:40Z' GROUP BY principal`
sofia: after hotfix deploy, we should run an automated remediation to strip inherited org roles created by the merge for principals that shouldn't have them. Create PR to add `rbacctl prune-inherited --since 2025-05-14T01:00Z --until 2025-05-14T03:00Z`
rahul: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/pull/4723 — includes unit tests and safety gate.
mike: canary shows expected behavior, membership resolver now returns canonical-only mapping on all shards. No further decrypts seen in canary logs.
sofia: escalate to security execs and legal? We exposed decrypt logs for a small subset (approx 9 decrypts across 3 tenants). We should notify impacted customers per policy.
rahul: logging the incident: incident-SEC-2025-05-14-01, severity P2. Draft notification with timeline + mitigation ready, will run through comms.
eva: followups: 1) add pre-deploy canary checks for principal mapping consistency, 2) add fast invalidation API to auth cache, 3) add audit rule to alert if org-level role grants appear for principals originating in a different workspace.
alex: also add KMS key access report (weekly) to detect anomalous cross-workspace decrypt patterns.
sofia: thanks team. tl;dr: bug in principal canonicalization + merge ordering allowed temporary org-level access for certain service principals; mitigated by token revocation, emergency deny, key rotation, resolver hotfix and remediation prune.
rahul: will follow up with postmortem + remediation checklist. Assigning owners: rahul (PM), mike (patch), eva (audit & notify), sofia (postmortem + comms), alex (remediation script).
sec-bot: Incident created: SEC-2025-05-14-01, link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-2025-01
